prompt: Protect an alcohol, do a reaction, deprotect. Starting material has a primary OH and we want to add a Grignard to a separate ester: 4-hydroxybutyl benzoate + (1) TMSCl/Et3N (protect OH as TMS ether); (2) 2 eq MeMgBr; (3) H3O+/TBAF (removes TMS). Draw the final product.

answers.label: A diol (ester reduced to 3° OH via 2 MeMgBr adds, phenol freed) and benzyl alcohol byproduct — but actually benzoyl side becomes PhC(Me)2OH

explanation: If you ran MeMgBr on the unprotected substrate, the free OH would quench the Grignard (acid-base). TMSCl protects the OH as a silyl ether (unreactive to Grignard). Then MeMgBr adds to the ester C=O twice: first add kicks out OR, second add gives a 3° alcohol. TBAF removes TMS. Products: 4-hydroxybutan-1-ol (the alcohol fragment that was the OR of the ester) + 2-phenyl-2-propanol (the newly formed 3° alcohol from the acyl side).
